The 'Title' column contains format headers like 'DVD' and 'Blu-Ray'. I will assign a new 'Format' column by forward-filling from these header rows, then filter Format == 'Blu-Ray' and compute the oldest year among those rows.
```python
# filename: assign_format_and_find_oldest_bluray.py
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

file_path = '/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/32102e3e-d12a-4209-9163-7b3a104efe5d.xlsx'
df = pd.read_excel(file_path, skiprows=2)
format_headers = {'DVD', 'Blu-Ray', 'VHS', 'CD', 'Digital'}

# Create Format column initialized as NaN
df['Format'] = np.nan
current_fmt = None
for i, t in df['Title'].items():
    val = str(t).strip()
    if val in format_headers:
        current_fmt = val
        df.at[i, 'Format'] = current_fmt
    else:
        df.at[i, 'Format'] = current_fmt

# Filter Blu-Ray entries (exclude the header row itself)
blu = df[(df['Format'] == 'Blu-Ray') & (~df['Title'].isin(format_headers))].copy()
blu['Year'] = pd.to_numeric(blu['Year'], errors='coerce')
blu = blu.dropna(subset=['Year'])
oldest_year = blu['Year'].min()
oldest_title = blu.loc[blu['Year'] == oldest_year, 'Title'].iloc[0]
print('Oldest Blu-Ray title:', oldest_title)
```
